subject: TheraHealth - limited training exception for analytics pipeline
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@therahealth.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 23 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Limited training carveout request for analytics pipeline

Soojin,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the walkthrough of Redwood Dedicated options. Legal reviewed the DPA draft and has one narrow ask we hope can be accepted: TheraHealth needs an explicit carveout stating that output/telemetry used by our analytics tooling may be retained for aggregate model analytics and quality monitoring, and that certain low-resolution, de-identified artifacts may be used to improve vendor-side models for non-personalized analytics.

Key constraints from our side:
- No customer PII (PHI) may be used for model training or shared outside the environment.
- Any training/analytics artifacts must be pseudonymized and sampled (<0.1% signal) and retained no longer than 90 days.
- TheraHealth requires an approval step from their security team before any telemetry export is enabled.

We flagged the request as an exception to your standard "no-training-on-customer-data" policy and attached a redline (TheraHealth_DPA_redline_v3.pdf) showing the exact language they propose. Can product/security confirm feasibility and supply an operational plan (controls, config toggles, audit trail) if Redwood were to agree to this narrow exception?

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gomez
Sr. Contracts Manager, TheraHealth
[Attachment: TheraHealth_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@therahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 26 Mar 2028 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Limited training carveout request for analytics pipeline

Maria —

Appreciate the clear ask and redline. Looping in Product (Lauren) and Security (Olga) to scope viability and operational guardrails. A few clarifying questions from the product side so we can scope engineering work and timeline: 

1) When you say "low-resolution, de-identified artifacts," can you give concrete examples of the exact fields or outputs you expect Redwood to export (e.g., token-level logits, prompt+response pairs, anonymized embeddings)?
2) Is TheraHealth OK with holding this behind a configurable feature flag per account that is disabled by default and requires signed DocuSign authorization?
3) For sampling, are you prescribing sampling on the request surface (TheraHealth-side gateway) or do you expect Redwood to perform sampling inside the runtime?

Operational ask: if Security approves, Product will want to offer this as an "opt-in analytics export" with a clear retention TTL and a per-account audit trail. Olga — could you confirm high-level controls you would need (KMS, audit log retention, access controls, support for legal hold) to consider this exception?

We'll aim for a proposed control list and implementation plan by end of week.

- Soojin
Soojin Lee
Manager, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@therahealth.com>, TheraHealth Legal <legal@therahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Limited training carveout request for analytics pipeline

Team / Maria —

Security has reviewed the proposed redline and the high-level ask. Short answer: we can support a tightly-scoped, auditable export pipeline, but only under these non-negotiable controls: 

- Export opt-in must be per-account and enforced by the control plane; default OFF.
- Exports limited to derived telemetry only: embeddings, anonymized aggregate metrics, and sampling of full (prompt,response) traces only after server-side PII scrubbing. No raw request bodies containing PHI allowed.
- Sampling must be deterministic and rate-limited on our side to ensure the <0.1% aggregate signal; implement reservoir sampling at the runtime exit point.
- All exported artifacts encrypted with customer-specific KMS keys (Bring-Your-Own-Key optional). Key rotations logged; decryption requires role-based access with MFA.
- Retention TTL configurable per account with an upper bound of 90 days; automated purge and immutable retention logs.
- Full audit trail (who/when/what) surfaced to both Redwood and TheraHealth via read-only audit exports; support for legal hold via documented workflow.
- No downstream usage for vendor model training without explicit separate consent and a tracked approval process.

Open product questions for Lauren: can the console UI expose an "Export analytics" toggle with the above constraints and a Data Use Agreement acceptance flow? Also need an engineering estimate for reservoir sampling and per-account KMS workflow.

If TheraHealth signs the DocuSign (linked) agreeing to the operational controls + the DPA carveout wording, Security will provisionally approve, pending an engineering playbook and a one-week pilot with monitoring.

- Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: analytics-data-flow-diagram.png (png)]

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@therahealth.com>, TheraHealth Legal <legal@therahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 28 Mar 2028 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Limited training carveout request for analytics pipeline

Maria —

Thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps: 

1) Product + Security can support the narrow analytics/training carveout under the controls Olga outlined (per-account opt-in, runtime PII scrubbing, reservoir sampling, KMS encryption, 90-day TTL, audit exports, explicit DocuSign consent).
2) Lauren will scope the console change (UI toggle + DUA acceptance) and provide an engineering estimate — target: draft spec by 2028-04-04.
3) Security requires a one-week pilot with monitoring before broader enablement. We will only enable exports for TheraHealth after DocuSign signature (link below).
4) Action items:
   - TheraHealth: review and sign DocuSign: https://docusign.com/therahealth/ENVELOPE-8877 (Maria)
   - Product: draft spec for opt-in flow and retention controls (Lauren)
   - Security: provide runtime sampling and scrubbing implementation notes (Olga)
   - Solutions: schedule pilot kickoff and prepare test dataset (Soojim/Aditya)

If everyone is aligned, we can move to DocuSign this week and have a pilot the week after. Maria — can you confirm you have the internal security approval for a one-week pilot window starting 2028-04-11?

Best,
Soojim (cc’ed team)
Soojin Lee
Manager, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
